static_traits.name: Wang Jie
static_traits.social_status: Has friends to play games with, but not yet discussed these emotional reactions with them
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; no similar problems in the past; not yet received psychotherapy or counseling
static_traits.language_features: Direct and clear expression, able to describe emotions and automatic thoughts concretely; able to collaborate with the counselor and self-observe; often uses 'black-and-white' expressions and catastrophizing language in gaming contexts; speech rate and logic Not mentioned; Neutral attitude

basic_info.main_problem: I am seeking counseling to cope with intense emotional reactions when failing at video games. The problem started last night when I lost three games in a row in my favorite game, which led me to take out the game disc and smash it, showing a strong negative emotional reaction. I believe the stress of failure triggered this reaction. This behavior has been escalating recently, and I tend toward all-or-nothing thinking when facing game challenges.
basic_info.core_demands: 'As long as it stops me from feeling this way every time I lose a game, I am willing to try.'; and realizing 'this behavior may be problematic and the underlying issues need addressing'.

core_beliefs: I have always been terrible at this game
Failing means I should not keep trying

special_situations.event: Lost three games in a row in a favorite game last night
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I keep Losing consecutive matches, it proves I am terrible and there is no point in continuing to play
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immediately quitting the game and smashing the disc to avoid further failure and Emotional loss of control
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will always be terrible; there is simply no way to win again, and continuing to play is pointless

special_situations.event: Losing a match when playing online with friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not win, it means I am not good enough; I am also responsible for the team's failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Loses temper with friends or distances from them, plays together less to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They will think It is all my fault; I am awful

special_situations.event: Focuses only on failures and mistakes when reviewing game performance after a match
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only winning counts as a good performance; nothing else is worth mentioning
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: negate or ignore past Good performances and the fun games brought
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Previous good performances do not count; I am just terrible

special_situations.event: After losing a match, emotions run high; prepares to rest yet cannot fall asleep
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Failure means serious consequences; it will make the whole night and tomorrow worse
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Immersed in negative emotions and failure imagery, hard to self-soothe
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is like the end of the world; everything is terrible

core_conflict.wish: Longing to Gaining recognition and self-worth through victory (seeing game performance as part of identity)
core_conflict.fear: Fears failure leading to shame and the collapse of self-worth (feels like 'the end of the world')
defense_goal: Maintaining control and Self-protection in an all-or-nothing way, avoiding further failure and shame by stopping the game and destroying the disc

object_relations.self_representation: When failing, regarding oneself as a 'bad player / failure'
object_relations.object_representation: Experiencing teammates/friends as others who might judge oneself (the other will blame or look down on oneself)

manifestations: Having 'what's the point' type thoughts when losing (not trying again, smashing the disc)
Binds game performance to identity; winning and losing are magnified into proof of existential worth

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Strong self-blame and self-deprecation after losing a game ('I will always be terrible')
Magnifying 'losing once' into 'it is meaningless, should not try again'

exception_events.target_problem: When losing video games, the client typically experiences Emotional loss of control, wholesale self-negation, and impulsive acts (e.g., smashing discs), followed by Sleep disturbed and snapping at friends.
exception_events.unique_outcome: At Work, when mistakes happen the client corrects them promptly and continues Work, without the intense loss of control or Self-denial seen in games.
exception_events.reason: Different context: mistakes at Work are seen as less 'personal'; different approach: focusing on problem-solving rather than win/loss judgment; hence emotions were more manageable and the outcome better.

positive_force: In work situations, able to adopt problem-solving strategies and maintain emotional stability
Having some self-observation ability, able to identify and describe negative automatic thoughts
Willing to try new methods and cooperate with counseling (willing to record and practice)
Has some social support (friends who game together)
negative_force: negate positive experiences (ignoring past Good performances and gaming fun)
Personalization and internalizing failure as low self-worth
Strongly binds game performance to self-identity, causing wins and losses to be excessively amplified
Lacks effective emotion regulation and coping strategies; after failure, strongly loses control, affecting sleep and interpersonal relations

target_behavior.behavior: Strong Emotional loss of control and Impulsively damaging objects (e.g., smashing discs) after losing games
antecedent: Still immersed in failure emotions after the match
target_behavior.core_reason: Strongly tying winning/losing to self-worth, with black-and-white and catastrophizing/predicting-the-future cognitions ('never going to win'), triggering shame and Sense of frustration, lacking effective emotion regulation strategies
target_behavior.function: Avoiding unpleasant emotions and seeking brief control / release of Sense of frustration
target_behavior.consequence: Losing gaming equipment and fun, further worsened mood, Sleep disturbed

target_behavior.behavior: Snapping at friends/teammates or feeling intense frustration after game failures, affecting Interpersonal relationships
antecedent: Losing a match in online multiplayer
Teammates making mistakes or matches not going smoothly
target_behavior.core_reason: Personalization and mind-reading explanations (attributing failure to herself, assuming negative evaluations from others), evaluating self-worth by winning and losing
target_behavior.function: Reducing self-blame and shame through outward venting and blaming others
target_behavior.consequence: Tense relationships with friends, reduced social support, further intensifying negative emotional experiences
